newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: ELEVEN PASSENGERS RELEASED FROM HOSPITAL AFTER TURBULENCE
Eleven of twelve people injured on a Singapore Airlines flight as it approached Sydney last night have been released from hospital.
One woman remains in Sydney's Prince of Wales hospital with leg injuries.
The Airbus was met by 10-ambulances when it arrived about half-past-eight after running into turbulence about an hour out of sydney.
A Singapore Airlines representative says the nine passengers and three crew injured were moving about the plane at the time.
UNION SAYS THE COMMUNITY WILL BE UNHAPPY WITH TELSTRA SALE
The Communication Workers' Union says consumers will be unhappy with the reduction in services from a commercially operated Telstra.
This follows a deal which will see Tasmania and Queensland benefit from upgraded telephone facilities as part of the Senate compromise over the part-sale of Telstra.
After securing the support of Tasmanian Independent Brian Harradine, and Queensland Independent, Mal Colston the Government will now get the Telstra sale bill through the Upper House.
The Opposition and Democrats have accused the Government of striking a crude political deal with the two Independents.
Union secretary Colin Cooper says the government will pay the penalty as consumers will be unhappy with the reduction in services from a commercially operated Telstra.
BLACKHAWK REPORT EXPECRED IN THE NEW YEAR

The report from the Blackhawk Board of Inquiry won't be released until the beginning of next year when the Defence Force and the Minister have worked how they'll implement its findings. The Inquiry into the Blackhawk disaster, which killed 18 soldiers when two helicopters collided near Townsville in June, finished sitting yesterday.
The Board will now consider the evidence of 144 witnesses and produce a report on the cause of accident and make recommendations to prevent a repetition.
The report will go to the Chief of the General Staff on December 20 and will then be examined by senior Defence Force Personnel.
Only after, its worked out how to implement the recommendations will the report be made public.
YOUNG ARTISTS WINS PRESTIGIOUS ART PRIZE
One of Australia's major prizes for religious art has been awarded to 29 year old Rachel Ellis, for her work entitled Woman at Jesus' Feet.
Ms Ellis was chosen last night as the 1996 recipient of the Blake Prize, ahead of leading names in the field including John Coburn and Joe Furlonger.
The Blake Prize was established 45 years ago to promote a greater understanding of all forms of religious art.
This year there were more than 300 entries, and a selection is on display at the State Library of New South Wales until the 19th of January.
